title: API: multi-invoker surface and deterministic result-merge for parallel function calls
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers reported intermittent mis-merged outputs when the API invoked multiple external tools/functions in parallel with streaming enabled. OpenAI-compatible function-calling semantics exposed a gap: parallel invocations could return overlapping structured outputs and partial streams that were hard to deterministically merge, and retries sometimes duplicated injected results. This PR introduces a new public-facing invocation layer (the 'multi-invoker' surface) and an internal deterministic result-merge contract so SDKs and the OpenAI compatibility adapter can reliably compose parallel tool/fn calls, preserve ordered structured output, and apply idempotent retries.

What changed (high level): added a multi-invoker API on the runtime that accepts a list of invocation descriptors and an explicit merge strategy; introduced per-invocation idempotency keys and result fingerprints; implemented a deterministic merge algorithm (priority by declared order, stable merge for structured sections, explicit conflict markers for ambiguous fields); updated the OpenAI compatibility adapter to translate function_call batching into multi-invoker descriptors and to map merged structured outputs back to function return values; added backpressure controls and a soft-concurrency limit so streaming connections do not exceed safe parallelism thresholds; improved retry semantics so retries are routed only when a fingerprint mismatch indicates transient failure.

Backward compatibility: default behavior preserves current single-invocation semantics. The multi-invoker is opt-in via a new parameter on the generation/chat endpoints (multi_invocations: boolean and merge_strategy: string). When clients don't opt in, the runtime behavior is unchanged. SDKs are updated to expose a convenience wrapper for multi-invoker usage with sensible defaults.

Testing and stability: unit tests cover merge determinism, fingerprint generation, idempotent retry cases, and streaming interleaving in synthetic workloads. e2e tests exercise the OpenAI function-calling compatibility with parallel fixturized handlers. Integration tests ran against Dedicated clusters to validate backpressure behavior under realistic concurrency patterns.

Docs and examples: new doc pages describe the multi-invoker surface, merge strategies (ordered, field-prefer, last-write), best-practice patterns for structured outputs, and migration notes for SDK users. Example showing parallel embeddings->rerank->formatter pipeline included in examples/multi_invoker/.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial multi-invoker API and types; deterministic merge implementation; openai adapter mapping; SDK convenience wrapper + tests; docs and example additions.

+++ src/compat/openai/adapter.py: transform function_call list into MultiInvokerRequest; map merged output back into function_return value
+++ sdk/python/redwood/multi_invoker.py: convenience wrapper and examples in docstrings
review_discussion:
Jonah Rivera: 'This surface looks promising. Can you clarify how we avoid duplicate streaming fragments when two invocations write to the same structured section?'
Avery Chen: 'We generate a per-invocation fingerprint and tag streaming chunks with a coalescing id; the merge step drops duplicate chunks from retries and uses declared order for deterministic placement.'
Priya Singh: 'Please add a test that simulates a slow secondary invocation that arrives after the primary finishes (race) — we need to ensure ordered merge still holds.'
Avery Chen: 'Added e2e test openai_function_parallel.test.ts that simulates late-arriving results and validates ordered merge semantics.'
Luca Marino: 'One nit: the API surface naming is slightly ambiguous — consider multi_invocations vs invocation_list. Not blocking.'
Avery Chen: 'Renamed the param to multi_invocations for clarity per review.'
CI: Integration tests initially failed on Dedicated cluster (flaky backpressure). Investigated: default soft_concurrency_limit was too high for our test cluster. Lowered limit and added backpressure throttling and a retry window; re-ran CI and all checks passed.

release_notes:
- New multi-invoker API to orchestrate parallel function/tool calls and deterministically merge structured outputs.
- OpenAI compatibility adapter updated to batch function calls and return merged function results.
- Safety: idempotent retry semantics and backpressure controls to avoid duplicate streaming fragments.
- SDKs: convenience wrappers in Python/TS and example multi-step pipelines.
notes_for_backport: No backport required for patch releases; feature gated behind API param. Consider backporting docs and SDK compatibility patches to the 2026.1 enterprise branch if customers request early access.
